title: Per-tenant silent eval runner with local-only goldens and selective telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a per-tenant ‘silent eval runner’ that executes customer-specific eval suites inside Dedicated/Private deployments without exporting any raw customer data off-host. The runner must: (1) run golden-set comparisons locally (encrypted at rest), (2) only emit aggregated, differentially-minimized telemetry or hashes, and (3) act as a blocking gate for config or model rollouts when regression thresholds are crossed. Goal is to enable model/config rollouts for tenants with strict data isolation requirements while preserving Redwood’s ability to detect regressions and trigger rollbacks or canaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a dedicated tenant, the eval runner can be configured per-tenant and scheduled automatically on model/config change. 2) Golden sets reside on the tenant's VPC or on-prem storage, encrypted with customer-managed keys. 3) Telemetry exported to Redwood control plane is limited to: pass/fail summary, aggregate delta metrics (no raw tokens), stable hash anchors for traceability (one-way), and a signed attestation stating eval environment and runner version. 4) Console UI shows tenant-level eval results and an option to block rollouts when thresholds are exceeded. 5) Security review completed and documented; no raw customer prompts or outputs leave the tenant boundary in any rollout path.
notes: Scope is intentionally narrow: first MVP targets embedding similarity and generation-level QA for controlled prompt families (<=50 golden prompts per tenant). Later phases will extend to structured-output checks and latency-sensitive micro-evals. We'll reuse the existing runner orchestration from ENG-42110 but add a privacy shim and attestation flow. Consider HSM/KMS integration for key wrapping in Private deployments.
comments: 2026-02-25 - PM sync: agreed on per-tenant scheduling and that golden sets must never be copied to Redwood-managed blob storage unless explicitly opted-in by the customer.

2026-03-01 - Eng design review (Liam): prototype runner will mount customer NFS/S3-compatible store, run evals in isolated container, and emit only signed JSON summary. Action: create ENG spike to validate mount performance (ENG-43822).
2026-03-04 - Security note (Priya Rao): require threat model for signed summary payloads, ensure hashes use salt and HMAC with tenant key. Also require a legal review for telemetry opt-in language.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback (Marco Silva): Console needs a binary pass/fail indicator and a drift slider to visualize regressions across model versions. Link to mockups: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Per-Tenant+Silent+Eval+Console+Mockups
2026-03-10 - Product follow-up: schedule milestone to gate dedicated rollouts; integration test plan drafted at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gSilentEvalTestPlan

2026-03-11 - Dependency update: ENG-42110 rollout hooks will expose a webhook that the runner can call with signed attestation. Adding ENG-45299 to instrument rollback automation if triggered by tenant gate.
2026-03-12 - Risk: running heavy evals inside tenant networks could increase customer infra costs; propose a pricing addendum for on-prem eval cycles.
